title: Fire Emblem's Creator Got Sued by Nintendo
hook:
Shouzou Kaga made the first five Fire Emblem games, then left and built a PlayStation rival that sold 345,000 copies in three months. Nintendo sued and mostly lost. Would you play a Fire Emblem made without Nintendo?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know the creator of Fire Emblem left Nintendo, made his own version, and got sued for it? Shouzou Kaga worked on the first five Fire Emblem games, from the 1990 original through Thracia 776 in 1999. After that fifth game he left Intelligent Systems and started a studio called Tirnanog. His new project was announced as Emblem Saga, a strategy RPG for the Sony PlayStation. Nintendo objected to the name, saying it would confuse players into thinking it was Fire Emblem. About six weeks before launch the title changed to Tear Ring Saga, and the Fire Emblem references were removed. Enterbrain published it in Japan on May twenty fourth, 2001. It sold more than 345,000 copies in its first three months. Nintendo sued that July anyway, asking for over two hundred fifty eight million yen and a halt to sales. In November 2002 the Tokyo District Court threw out Nintendo's claims. On appeal in 2004, Enterbrain was ordered to pay seventy six million yen. But the game was not ruled a copyright breach, and it stayed on shelves. Japan's Supreme Court upheld that in 2005. Kaga has never worked on Fire Emblem again. Would you play a Fire Emblem made without Nintendo? Follow for more gaming history.
